newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded, prompt OTC levels still firm.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded, prompt OTC levels still firm.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract did not trade on Monday morning, a pattern which has become common in recent weeks.
All Monday morning sessions since June 9 have seen no trade.
At the close there were no bids or offers on front months August and September. October saw a bid/offer spread of 11.00/11.20 pence a therm compared with a previous settlement price of 11.00 pence.

Traders on the OTC market said prompt prices remained firm following terminal problems on Friday afternoon at Bacton and Theddlethorpe which pushed up short-term prices. There were reports that day ahead gas had traded at 10.50 pence a therm.
A dealer said problems affecting Bacton and Theddlethorpe appeared to have been resolved, and gas was flowing freely from St Fergus on Monday morning as it had been over the weekend.

But problems had caused a temporary spike on Friday and the flexibility mechanism was said to have bought at over 40 pence a therm on Friday evening. It was also reported to have sold twice on Sunday at levels below nine pence a therm as the problems were resolved.
